programme: An HLF-gated haematopoietic stem/progenitor differentiation module: HLF marks stem-cell maintenance and feeds into lineage-committing factors — CEBPE for granulocyte terminal differentiation, PAX5 for B-lymphoid commitment, CBFA2T3 (ETO2/MTG16) for the erythroid-megakaryocyte branch (its target EPB42 is an erythrocyte membrane-skeleton gene) — with ARNT supplying the hypoxia/EPO axis that couples erythropoiesis to oxygen sensing, E2F5-TFDP2 driving progenitor cell-cycle entry (MYC, PCNA, RFC3, ASF1B targets), and SMARCA5 providing the chromatin remodeling that opens these lineage loci, notably including other remodeler genes (SMARCA1, CHD1, INO80) among its own targets.
role_in_a: In psoriasis, skin lesions are sustained by continuous neutrophil recruitment (Munro microabscesses) and monocyte-derived inflammation; a bone-marrow programme biased toward granulocyte and myeloid output (CEBPE) with proliferative expansion of progenitors (E2F5/TFDP2) would explain a durable supply of inflammatory effector cells rather than a single acute burst.
role_in_b: In stroke, ischemia triggers emergency granulopoiesis and mobilization of haematopoietic stem/progenitor cells from marrow, hypoxia-driven induction of EPO and angiogenic genes (the ARNT/HIF axis), and a documented shift toward B cells with enhanced phagocytic and chemotactic capacity (PAX5-expressing lineage) in the post-stroke period.
shared_axis: Both conditions place chronic or acute systemic stress on the same HLF-gated progenitor pool, pushing it toward myeloid and lymphoid effector output rather than steady-state turnover; this is consistent with the established clinical observation that psoriasis carries elevated stroke risk, for which accelerated marrow-driven inflammatory cell production is one proposed mechanism.
reasoning: The eight carrying factors compose a nameable, non-arbitrary differentiation circuit (stem-cell maintenance → lineage commitment → proliferation → chromatin access), and it survives after generic immune/haematopoietic regulators (STAT2, STAT5B, TBX21, BCL6, EPAS1) were already stripped out as tissue-generic, so it is not simply rediscovering an obvious immune signal. But almost nothing in the retrieved record actually places this programme in either disease: only PAX5 has disease-specific literature, and only for stroke; no factor has any Open Targets or paper evidence for psoriasis; and recurrence for every carrying factor is mid-range (11-16 of 24), well short of near-universal. The account is plausible but rests on general knowledge of factor function, not on retrieved evidence for this pair.
support: PMID 37282471 — reports a B-cell phenotype with enhanced phagocytic and chemotactic capability following stroke, the only retrieved paper that places a carrying factor (PAX5-lineage) specifically in one of the two diseases; no papers or Open Targets associations were retrievable connecting any carrying factor to psoriasis.
how_to_falsify: Profile CD34+ progenitor composition and lineage output (CEBPE+ granulocyte precursors, PAX5+ pro-B cells, CBFA2T3+ erythroid precursors) by scRNA-seq or flow cytometry in matched psoriasis and post-stroke peripheral blood/marrow samples; if psoriatic myelopoiesis and post-stroke emergency haematopoiesis do not converge on a shared HLF-high progenitor expansion signature, or if SMARCA5/E2F5-TFDP2 chromatin and cell-cycle activity are not co-elevated with the lineage factors in both settings, the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: The two networks were built from different tissues (skin for psoriasis, blood for stroke), so this account crosses into bone marrow, a compartment not directly profiled by either network — it is an inference bridging the two, not a measurement in either tissue. Only 24 patient-group comparisons across 4 independent cohort pairs support the factor set, and no carrying factor exceeds 16/24. The single-view exclusions (FOXO4, MYBL2, IRF1, NFATC2, etc.) were each driven by one patient group and are rightly excluded. The tissue-generic exclusions removed several classical immune master regulators (STAT2, STAT5B, TBX21, BCL6, EPAS1), which is why the surviving set looks like a differentiation circuit rather than a generic inflammation signature — but this also means the more familiar, better-documented immune regulators were unavailable to anchor the story, leaving it thinner than it might otherwise appear.
